disclaimer: DISCLAIMER: This symptom checker is a rule-based triage tool for informational purposes only. It is NOT medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. If you are experiencing a life-threatening emergency, call Campus Police or 911 immediately.

questions.question: Are you experiencing severe shortness of breath, bluish lips, or acute chest pain?

yes.action: Call Campus Police (555-0100) or 911 immediately. Seek emergency room care.

questions.question: Is your temperature over 102°F (38.9°C) lasting more than 48 hours?

yes.action: Schedule an urgent same-day evaluation at Campus Student Health Clinic.

questions.question: Do you have mild sore throat, nasal congestion, and mild cough without difficulty breathing?

yes.action: Hydrate frequently, rest, use warm saline gargles, monitor temperature, and quarantine if contagious.

no.action: Call Campus Health advice nurse for personalized evaluation.

questions.question: Did the headache come on suddenly like a thunderclap, or is it accompanied by stiff neck, confusion, or weakness on one side?

yes.action: RED ALERT: Possible stroke or intracranial hemorrhage. Call 911 immediately.

questions.question: Did the headache follow a head bump, collision, or sports injury with dizziness or memory fog?

yes.action: Possible concussion. Stop activity, seek athletic trainer or health clinic within 2 hours.

no.action: Tension/dehydration headache: Drink 500ml water, rest in a dark quiet room, take approved OTC pain reliever.

questions.question: Is the pain severe and localized in the lower right abdomen, or accompanied by persistent vomiting and high fever?

yes.action: URGENT CARE ALERT: Possible acute appendicitis. Go to nearest Emergency Department.

no.action: Mild cramps/indigestion: Sip electrolyte fluids, eat bland foods (BRAT diet), avoid dairy/spicy foods.
